extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, committee managers, and counsel responsible for establishing, operating, and overseeing Federal advisory committees
extracted.subtask_description: Overview guidance on establishment, operation, subcommittees, transparency, and Secretariat responsibilities under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA). Aims to help agencies comply with statutory and regulatory requirements for advisory committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. chapter 10) governs the establishment, operation, and termination of advisory committees within the executive branch and defines what constitutes a Federal advisory committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act helps ensure that Congress and the public are kept informed regarding the number, purpose, membership, activities, and cost of advisory committees. GSA’s authority for administering FACA is contained in 5 U.S.C. 1006(c) and Executive Order 12024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and role of Federal advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal advisory committees may be composed of subject matter experts, representative members, and Federal Government employees who provide advice and recommendations to help inform and improve executive branch operations and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent any legislative requirements, advisory committees are advisory only. They furnish expert advice, ideas, and diverse opinions (5 U.S.C. 1002(a)) and deliberate to provide recommendations during meetings that operate under transparency laws promoting public access, input, and accountability. Member perspectives may come from consumers, technical experts, the public at-large, academia, business, or other sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee status rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A subcommittee is a sub-group that reports to a Federal advisory committee, not directly to a Federal officer or agency, whether or not its members are drawn from the parent committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a subcommittee makes advice or recommendations directly to a Federal officer or agency, it is no longer functioning as a subcommittee and must: file a charter following the requirements of § 102-3.70 that includes the information required in § 102-3.75; comply with all requirements of the FACA final rule; and will be counted as a chartered advisory committee at an agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to establish advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal advisory committee can be established under the authority of an agency head, statute, or Presidential Directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing authority determines whether a committee is discretionary or non-discretionary and affects who has legal discretion to create or terminate the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary advisory committee definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A discretionary advisory committee is established under the authority of an agency head or is authorized by statute in general (non-specific) language or Congressional committee report language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A discretionary committee’s establishment or termination is within the legal discretion of an agency head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discretionary advisory committee definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-discretionary advisory committee is required by statute or by Presidential Directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory non-discretionary committee is generally identified specifically in statute by name, purpose, or functions, and its establishment or termination is beyond the legal discretion of an agency head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretariat role: consultations on committee lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee Management Secretariat engages in consultations with agencies on the establishment, re-establishment, renewal, merger, and termination of Federal advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of GSA’s oversight to promote government-wide compliance with FACA and consistent handling of committee lifecycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretariat role: prescribe advice and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat prescribes advice and guidance applicable to Federal advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes interpretation of statutory and regulatory requirements and best practices for agency implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretariat role: assistance in implementation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat assists other agencies in implementing and interpreting the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support includes clarifying requirements, answering agency questions, and providing authoritative interpretations to promote consistent compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual comprehensive review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat conducts an annual comprehensive review of government-wide Federal advisory committee accomplishments, costs, benefits, and other indicators to measure performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review is intended to measure and report on committee performance and inform oversight and policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training development and provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat develops and provides government-wide training regarding the Act and related statutes and principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is aimed at agency staff and committee managers to improve understanding and compliance with FACA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for interagency coordination and legal counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat supports the Interagency Committee on Federal Advisory Committee Management and the FACA Attorney Council to improve compliance with the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support functions include coordination among agencies and provision of legal and policy advice to strengthen FACA adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA database design and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat designs and maintains a FACA database to facilitate data collection, reporting, and use of information required by the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The database supports transparency and statutory reporting obligations by centralizing required committee data (e.g., number, purpose, membership, activities, costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory development
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat prepares regulations on Federal advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations operationalize statutory requirements and the FACA final rule, providing binding agency obligations and procedural detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of performance measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretariat identifies performance measures that may be used to evaluate Federal advisory committee accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measures are intended to assess committee effectiveness, costs, benefits, and other indicators as part of government-wide oversight.
